title: Prior therapy defines mutation profiles in childhood cancer at relapse.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 18807964 file list and README (CC-BY-NC 4.0): SNV calls 285 MB gz, indel calls 69 MB gz (both over the 50 MB cap, not downloaded), SV calls 4.1 MB (opened: 45,693 rows, 583 samples). GitHub source_data opened: Fig_2.tsv = 611 tumours with Thr_State (Advanced-Treated 256, Primary-Naive 249, Primary-Treated 93, Advanced-Naive 13), tumour type (97 types), age, purity, mutation burdens; ExFig_4a.tsv = 611 samples x 40 SBS signature activities with Pre/Post-Therapy label; ExFig_7a/7b = SBS96/SBS1536 profiles for only 111 samples; Fig_4a = 141 platinum-treated tumours with days since exposure and signature Y/N (81/60). Treated fraction varies strongly by tumour type (neuroblastoma 78/88 treated, high-grade glioma 21/54).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Per-drug exposure and cumulative dose per patient (the paper's core labels) are described but not found in any public file: the repo's ml_model.py loads KZM_therapy_classes_NY.txt and KZM_md.tsv, which are absent from the repo; Europe PMC supplementary files timed out (supplement not retrievable). The ensemble classifier's F1 of 0.89 and its split come from the text; Hartwig and PROFYLE data are on-request only; raw reads are in EGA/dbGaP (controlled).

a1_downloadable.note: Processed variant calls on Zenodo and per-sample tables on GitHub download without login (checked). Raw reads are controlled access (EGA, dbGaP) but not needed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: treated-vs-naive status is a column (Thr_State in Fig_2.tsv, Treatment in ExFig_4a.tsv) for all 611 tumours. The more interesting per-drug exposure label is NOT in any public file I found; it would need the unretrieved supplementary tables.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: 40 signature activities per tumour already tabulated; raw SNV positions with ref/alt are on Zenodo, but building 96-channel spectra for all 611 needs the GRCh37 reference genome to get flanking bases.

a4_units_stated.note: Mutation counts and VAF (0-1) documented in Zenodo README; signature activities are mutation counts per signature (checked in file).

a5_enough_rows.note: 611 tumours, binary classification (349 treated / 262 naive), just above the ~400 classification bar. Per-drug subsets are much smaller (e.g. 141 platinum-treated with timing).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <10 MB for signature table; ~355 MB compressed if rebuilding spectra from SNV/indel calls
a6_fits_laptop.note: Tabular; trees or logistic regression on CPU in seconds.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 611 tumours in Fig_2 and ExFig_4a match the paper's 611; SV file has 583 samples, matching the 28 missing SV values in Fig_2.

a8_label_provenance.note: Treatment state comes from harmonized clinical re-annotation, not from the mutations. But the paper's own classifier target (platinum signature present Y/N) is computed from the mutation spectra, so that label is circular and must not be used.

B1.why: Label table (Fig_2) and signature table (ExFig_4a, long format) join on sample ID; 611/611 matched (checked).

B2.why: GitHub TSVs and SV file parsed first try with pandas (checked).

B3.why: Three programmes (KiCS, ZERO, MSK) sequenced separately; one shared pipeline per paper, batch effects unverified.

B4.why: Binary treated/naive label, no censored values; 2 missing ages, 1 missing purity (checked).

B5.why: Patients can contribute multiple tumours (Fig_1c lists patients with up to 8 samples); needs patient grouping.

B6.why: Zenodo README documents variant columns fully; GitHub source-data tables are undocumented figure exports.

C1.why: Treated-vs-naive is easy from burden alone; only 'residual exposure signal beyond known signatures' is informative.

C2.why: Paper's own open ensemble classifier (F1 0.89); Pich 2019 mapped therapy footprints on ~3,500 tumours.

C3.why: Weak 'better evaluation' angle: re-test paper's classifier with patient- and tumour-type-grouped splits.

C4.why: Exposure history is known clinically; value lies in detecting hidden mutagenic damage, not replacing records.

C5.why: Published F1 0.89 and PR/ROC source data in repo; mutation-burden-only dummy is obvious.

D1.why: No named open pretrained backbone for mutation-spectrum vectors identified or retrieved.

D2.why: No embedding step needed; plain models on 96-1536 features run on CPU.

D3.why: Zenodo data CC-BY-NC 4.0; paper CC BY-NC-ND; non-commercial use fine.

E1.why: Hold out whole patients and whole tumour types; Type column present in Fig_2 (checked).

E2.why: 15 tumour types with ≥10 samples per paper; 97 types in file.

E3.why: Majority class (57% treated), per-tumour-type rate, and burden-only logistic regression are computable.

E4.why: No replicate sequencing of the same tumour in public files.

E5.why: Known: SBS31/SBS35 platinum signatures must rank top for platinum-exposed tumours.

E6.why: Label shuffling and burden-only ablation are straightforward.

E7.why: POG adult cohort is published but counts only; Hartwig is on-request; no year column seen.

E8.why: Repo holds PR/ROC source data (pr_288.tsv, AP 0.95) and ml_model.py for the 111-sample classifier.

G1.why: GRCh37 coordinates, HGNC IDs and gene symbols in Zenodo variant files (README checked).

G2.why: COSMIC signatures and Hartwig metastatic cohort plausible, but Hartwig is access-restricted.

G3.why: Signature-to-COSMIC join is one-to-one by signature name.

G4.why: Paediatric-vs-adult footprint transfer is a modest question; paper already tested cosine 0.72 on POG.

H1.why: 262 treatment-naive tumours as negatives alongside 349 treated (checked).

H2.why: Three programmes, 97 tumour types, but all high-risk/relapsed paediatric precision-medicine cases.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below, limited to high-risk paediatric tumours with mixed regimens.

H4.why: Paper discusses cohort bias toward aggressive disease; tumour-type confounding not foregrounded.

I1.why: Paediatric oncology genomics groups (Shlien lab, SickKids); no named user decision.

I2.why: Could flag hidden platinum damage, but clinical decisions rest on exposure records.

I3.why: Treated-vs-naive AUC is a proxy; the real decision (de-escalation) needs per-drug labels.

I4.why: Mutation burden and SBS31/35 presence probably carry most signal; ML adds little.

J1.why: Grouped-split evaluation and ablations, but small tabular data, no transfer learning.

J2.why: Signature biology is well documented (COSMIC); clinical confounding needs an oncology collaborator.

J3.why: A grouped-split re-evaluation note is shareable; little beyond that.

J4.why: Roughly one week, not formally fixed.

existing_models.name: This paper's soft-voting ensemble (random forest, logistic regression, XGBoost, CatBoost) on SBS96/288/1536 features
existing_models.score_and_split: F1 0.89 for platinum-signature-positive vs negative among 111 platinum-treated tumours; F1 0.81-0.82 after removing known platinum channels; split not stated in what I read. Code in scripts/ml_model.py, PR/ROC data in repo.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: 27% of platinum-treated tumours lack detectable platinum signatures; whether hidden platinum damage exists beyond known signatures, and tracking resistant clones before expansion.

existing_models.name: Pich et al. 2019, 'The mutational footprints of cancer therapies' (Nature Genetics), signature extraction on ~3,500 Hartwig metastatic tumours
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a predictive classifier; signature-treatment association analysis in adult metastatic tumours.

backbone.name: none identified (mutation-spectrum vectors have no standard open pretrained backbone)

integration.partner_dataset: COSMIC mutational signature catalogue (open reference spectra); Hartwig metastatic cohort would be the large partner but needs a data request
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do chemotherapy footprints learned in children transfer to adult metastatic tumours treated with the same drugs?

controls.positive_control: SBS31/SBS35/DBS5 activity must be the top features for platinum-exposed tumours; mutation burden should separate treated from naive.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle treatment labels within tumour type; performance must fall to the per-tumour-type base rate.
controls.external_validation: None openly available: POG adult cohort (published supplementary counts) is partial; Hartwig and PROFYLE are on request.

honest_claim_h3: Among 611 high-risk paediatric tumours from three precision-medicine programmes, mutation-signature profiles separate previously treated from untreated tumours, but only to the extent the signal survives holding out whole tumour types and patients.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the pattern of DNA mutations in a child's tumour to predict whether, and with which drugs, the tumour was previously treated.
plain_idea.train_on: For each of 611 tumours (verified), the counts of mutations attributed to 40 known mutation patterns ('signatures'), or the full 96-category mutation spectrum rebuilt from the deposited variant calls.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the tumour had prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy (treated vs untreated), taken from the clinical records re-annotated by the authors; per-drug exposure would need tables not found publicly.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would show how much treatment-caused DNA damage is detectable beyond the known platinum signatures; even a negative result shows the separation is mostly tumour type and mutation count.

more_or_better_data.why: Our data is the paper's own 611 tumours, the same set its classifier used; Pich 2019 had ~3,500 adult tumours.

confidence_score.why: No replicate sequencing, so per-prediction noise cannot be estimated from the data.

models_beatable.why: The 2026 ensemble reports F1 0.89 on 111 samples with no stated grouped split; an honest patient/tumour-type split may lower it, but that is re-evaluation, not beating it.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No accessible new data measuring the same exposure the same way: Hartwig and PROFYLE are on request, and POG offers only partial published counts.

label_elsewhere.sources: Hartwig Medical Foundation metastatic cohort has treatment histories (known resource, access by request); POG adult cohort supplementary data (cited in paper, not checked).
label_elsewhere.why: An external cohort with treatment labels would test whether paediatric therapy footprints generalise, but none is openly downloadable.

risks: Several tumours from the same patient (up to 8 per patient in Fig_1c) could land in both train and test.
Treatment status is heavily tied to tumour type (neuroblastoma 78/88 treated, high-grade glioma 21/54), so the model may learn tumour type.
Treated tumours are mostly 'Advanced' relapses from specific programmes, so programme or sequencing batch may correlate with the label.
The paper's own signature Y/N label is computed from the same spectra and must not be used as a target.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole patients (patient ID partly visible in Fig_1c; sample IDs carry patient prefixes, not fully verified), plus leave-tumour-type-out evaluation using the Type column seen in Fig_2.tsv.
checks: Shuffle labels within tumour type and confirm collapse to the per-type base rate.
Train on tumour type plus total mutation burden alone and compare with the full model.
Train on programme prefix (KiCS/zcc/I-H) alone to measure batch leakage.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable for patient leakage, but tumour-type and stage confounding is a serious risk that may explain most of the signal.

success_criteria.metric: AUROC (area under the receiver-operating curve) for treated vs naive under leave-tumour-type-out, because the question is whether therapy damage is detectable independent of cancer type.
success_criteria.baselines: Majority class 57% treated (computed from Fig_2); per-tumour-type rate and burden-only logistic regression (to compute); paper's F1 0.89 is for a different, circular target.
success_criteria.success: AUROC at least 0.10 above the tumour-type-plus-burden baseline under leave-tumour-type-out; exact baseline value unknown until computed.
success_criteria.kill: If signature features add under 0.05 AUROC over tumour type plus mutation burden on the first afternoon, stop.

ambitious.why: Publishes cancer genomics methods; would need a clear demonstration of hidden therapy damage beyond known signatures that transfers to adult tumours.

realistic.journal: Bioinformatics (application note) or PLOS Computational Biology
realistic.why: A grouped-split re-evaluation of therapy-exposure prediction from mutation spectra fits a short methods/benchmark note.

fallback.why: A negative result (signal is mostly tumour type and burden) is still worth a short preprint.

pitch.headline: 611 childhood tumours, each labelled treated or untreated from clinical records, with 40 mutation-signature counts already tabulated and open.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Paediatric whole genomes with harmonized therapy annotation across 97 tumour types, 262 untreated negatives, and processed variant calls under CC-BY-NC; per-drug doses are described in the paper but not found in public files.
pitch.the_win: Showing treated-vs-untreated is detectable at AUROC well above a tumour-type-plus-burden baseline when whole tumour types are held out.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn that the published classifier's signal is largely tumour type and mutation count, a useful caution for therapy-footprint claims.
pitch.who_wants_it: Paediatric cancer genomics groups (the Shlien lab at SickKids, ZERO Childhood Cancer, MSK) weighing therapy de-escalation evidence.

ml_idea: Re-evaluate prediction of prior therapy exposure from tumour mutation signatures (611 paediatric genomes) with patient- and tumour-type-grouped splits, ablating mutation burden and tumour type, and running the authors' open ensemble as baseline.

effort.compute_note: Estimated: signature table is 611 x 40; rebuilding full 96-channel spectra from the 285 MB SNV file would add ~1 day and a GRCh37 reference download.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Fit treated-vs-naive with tumour type plus total mutation burden only, leave-tumour-type-out, and see how much 40 signature activities add.

verdict_reason: Part A passes for treated-vs-untreated (611 rows, verified), but that label is confounded by tumour type and easy from mutation burden, the per-drug exposure labels that would make it interesting are not public, there's no backbone, and the paper already ships an open classifier.
